chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: The explanation of the rare expressions in this sermon.

His words (peace be upon him): 'Our mountains cracked' means they split due to drought. It is said 'the garment cracked' when it tore. It is also said 'the vegetation cracked' or 'it dried and withered' when it dried up and became dry. All of it means the same.
ai.seo_question: What does the word 'insāḥat' mean in the context of the Sermon of Seeking Rain?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī elucidates the rare term 'insāḥat' in the Sermon of Seeking Rain, interpreting it as the earth cracking from extreme drought. He supports this by drawing linguistic parallels to torn garments and withered vegetation, emphasizing the physical manifestation of aridity in the landscape. This exegesis highlights the Imam's precise use of metaphor to convey the severity of the environmental crisis facing the community.
